_layerNote: Only L1 (deterministic unit) is used. Every claim here is a nil-pointer dereference on a plain struct field, fully determined by the in-process object graph -- envtest or a live cluster would add cost and flakiness without adding proof. L2/L3 deliberately skipped.

findings.claim: With PR #6157 applied, a DataLoad against a CacheRuntime whose CacheRuntimeClass omits `topology` still panics at dataload.go:97 (nil deref of runtimeClass.Topology.Worker). The DataLoad controller is a separate entry point; transform.go's Topology==nil guard is not on its call graph.
findings.contradicts: PR description: 'cm.go is the only place in the repo where this nil check is missing.'

findings.claim: Same defect class at image.go:29 (getDataOperationImage derefs runtimeClass.Topology.Worker with no Topology==nil guard). Same DataLoad path as F1; F1 panics a few lines earlier, so this one is independently unsafe but not independently reachable today.

sync.go:190/214 deref runtimeClass.Topology with no Topology==nil guard. LATENT, not live: on the Sync path PR #6157's own new error (raised earlier, at sync.go:55 -> cm.go) short-circuits Sync before syncRuntimeSpec runs. It becomes live if that ordering changes.
The Master and Worker guards added by this PR have no regression coverage: reverting either leaves the cm.go test selection green. Confirms Copilot's review comment on cm_test.go:253.
findings._note: Not a runtime canary -- proven by mutation, not by a test that runs in this harness. re-verify.sh will report it as Harness-update; re-run the mutation script by hand for this one.

findings.claim: The new `all three components nil` error branch is untested -- only `Topology == nil` is covered. Reverting the all-nil clause leaves the suite green. Confirms Copilot's review comment on cm_test.go:271.

harnessBitesCheck.method: Applied the proposed fix (add `runtimeClass.Topology != nil &&` at dataload.go:97, image.go:29, sync.go:190, sync.go:214), re-ran the canaries, then reverted.
harnessBitesCheck.result: All four canaries flipped to RED under the fix and returned to GREEN after revert. Production diff back to the PR patch only.

baselineNoise.warning: The package's Ginkgo suite (TestCacheEngine) shows 12 pre-existing spec failures on the base used here, IDENTICAL with and without the PR patch -- so they are NOT caused by PR #6157 and must not be reported as findings. Consequence: never use whole-package pass/fail as a mutation signal; it yields a false 'all guards covered' result. Use `-run 'TestGenerateRuntimeConfigData'` / `-run 'TestVerifyF'`, which are green at baseline.
